sources.note: QL5/QL1 Owner's Manual d1 (opened, text read): QL1 dimensions 468 mm x 272 mm x 562 mm (W x H x D); fader 100 mm motorized; rear panel p.16-17 (XLR-3-31 INPUT 1-16 female, XLR-3-32 OMNI OUT 1-8 male, Dante PRIMARY/SECONDARY etherCON, AC IN, power switch); Selected Channel [PAN] knob adjusts pan or L/R balance; an [ON] key on every strip; USER DEFINED keys. The manual's dimension drawing carries no connector coordinates, so every position below is read from the photos.

Rear, straight-on (assets-source/yamaha-ql1/photos/rear.jpg, 2000x1281). The rear panel is the io face: all 7 modelled ports and the power switch are on it. Picture and numbers use ONE mapping (re-measured 2026-11-10, Wave 3): the picture of the io face is the crop 128,132,1731,1006 of this photo (the product spans x 153..1833 and y 132..1137, padded 25 px each side), so 1731 px = 468 mm and 1006 px = 272 mm: 3.6987 px/mm in both directions, y from the bottom of the feet (px 1137). Cross-checks of that scale on the panel itself: the Neutrik D-size etherCON flange is 95.7 x 115 px = 25.9 x 31.1 mm (26 x 31 published), the power rocker housing 76 x 125 px = 20.6 x 33.8 mm. Port = the centre of the connector read on a zoomed crop (+/- 1.5 px = +/- 0.4 mm): INPUT 1 and 2 (top row of the right-hand block, input 1 rightmost seen from behind, pitch 23.4 mm), OMNI OUT 1, 2, 3 = out-main-l, out-main-r, out-mix-1 (right-hand end of the male block on the left, pitch 25.5 mm; the catalog simplifies, which OMNI OUT carries which bus is a guess), PRIMARY etherCON = dante-primary, AC IN (IEC C14) = power-in, power = the rocker above the AC inlet (protrusion d = 8 mm is an estimate). The earlier positions (3.68 px/mm about the body centre, y from px 1160) put the XLR rows 8.5 mm, the etherCON 5.5 mm and the inlet 6.4 mm too high on the stretched picture.

Same rear photo, read for the body (Wave 3): the two option-slot plates SLOT 2 (left) and SLOT 1 (right) are dark plates 121 x 40 mm at x 193.6 and 320.6 mm, y 15.7 to 55.7 mm (px 844..1292 / 1314..1761, y 931..1079), modelled as 1.2 mm recesses (the depth is an estimate); the body underside is at 12.7 mm (px 1090) and the four feet are 12.7 mm tall, 21.6 mm across at the body and about 15.5 mm at the table, centred 41.8 mm from the sides (the rear pair measured; 28 mm from the front and rear edges is an estimate).

Front, elevated (assets-source/yamaha-ql1/photos/front.jpg, 2448x2216), read for the body (Wave 3): the phones panel (level knob and jack) is a recessed panel about 100.6 x 22 mm at 335.6 mm from the left edge on the lower front face (modelled 2 mm deep, an estimate), the top plate has a thick rounded front edge (the arm rest, modelled as a 14 mm roll) and the lower body is set back under it (3/4 photo: about 5 mm at the sides, base 30 mm tall above the feet, estimates). Brand marks are not modelled.

Top, overhead (assets-source/yamaha-ql1/photos/top.jpg, 1689x2000): x scale 3.006 px/mm and y scale 3.062 px/mm, calibrated to the 468 mm width and 562 mm depth; top-face y runs from the rear (I/O) edge to the front. The photo has the rear at the TOP of the picture, but the face-local convention for a top face is seen from above with the I/O edge (the rear) at the BOTTOM, x right, y up: that is the photo rotated 180 degrees, so the photo x is mirrored, xMm = 468 - x_photo (photo x = (px - 140) / 3.006: fader/mute A 401.5 -> 66.5, PAN 337.7 -> 130.3, USER key 1 411.8 -> 56.2); y is already measured from the rear edge and is unchanged. Control mapping: fader-master = master fader A of the Master section (100 mm travel, position at mid-travel); mute-master = the [ON] key above fader A (it switches the channel on or off); balance-master = the Selected Channel [PAN] knob (manual: it adjusts pan or L/R balance); playback-usb = USER DEFINED key 1: the catalog id is logical-only, the console has no dedicated play button, user keys can be assigned to recorder functions, key 1 is the stand-in. Heights (h) of caps, knobs and keys are estimates, not visible in the overhead view.

Neutrik NC3FD-L-1 product page (opened): "Standardized D sized 24 mm panel cutout". The XLR receptacles in the photos are Neutrik D-series (NEUTRIK legible on the Rio3224-D2 front), so openingMm = 24 for the XLR ports. The NC3MD-L-1 (male) page says the same (https://www.neutrik.com/en/product/nc3md-l-1).
